source_metadata.exact_title: Comparing Effectiveness and Safety of SGLT2 Inhibitors vs DPP-4 Inhibitors in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Varying Baseline HbA1c Levels
source_metadata.source_type: Original Investigation; observational new-user comparative effectiveness and safety study
source_metadata.data_source: Deidentified Optum Clinformatics Data Mart Database with linked outpatient laboratory results

atoms.canonical_statement: The study compared cardiovascular effectiveness and safety of SGLT2i versus DPP-4i in adults with type 2 diabetes overall and across baseline HbA1c levels.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To compare cardiovascular effectiveness and safety of treatment with SGLT2i vs DPP-4i

atoms.canonical_statement: The investigators used a new-user comparative effectiveness and safety design in a nationwide US commercial/Medicare Advantage claims database with linked laboratory data.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We performed a new-user comparative effectiveness and safety research study using a US health insurance data set

atoms.canonical_statement: Outpatient laboratory results were available for approximately 45% of beneficiaries; a feasibility analysis compared eligible patients with versus without recent HbA1c values.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: performed a feasibility analysis comparing baseline characteristics of eligible patients with vs. without an HbA1c value

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible patients were adults with type 2 diabetes who newly initiated SGLT2i or DPP-4i and had at least one HbA1c result within 3 months before initiation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: eligible patients had to have at least 1 recorded diagnosis of T2D and an HbA1c laboratory result

population.label: Eligible new users with T2D
inclusion_criteria: HbA1c result within 3 months before cohort entry

atoms.canonical_statement: Key exclusions included end-stage kidney disease/dialysis/transplant, selected malignancy, nursing-home residence, type 1 diabetes, and secondary or gestational diabetes.
The eligible cohort included 144,614 adults: 60,523 SGLT2i initiators and 84,091 DPP-4i initiators; mean age was 62 years and 54% were male.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A total of 144 614 eligible adults (mean [SD] age, 62 [12.4] years; 54% male participants)

population.label: Eligible adults with T2D initiating SGLT2i or DPP-4i

atoms.canonical_statement: After 1:1 propensity-score matching, 87,274 patients remained, with 43,637 patients in each treatment group.
The matched HbA1c <7.5% subgroup contained 24,052 patients; the reported mean HbA1c was 6.8%.
The matched HbA1c 7.5%-9% subgroup contained 32,290 patients; the reported mean HbA1c was 8.2%.
The matched HbA1c >9% subgroup contained 30,932 patients; the reported mean HbA1c was 10.6%.
The exposure was initiation of an SGLT2 inhibitor.

exposures.details: new initiation of an SGLT2 inhibitor

atoms.canonical_statement: The active comparator was initiation of a DPP-4 inhibitor.

exposures.details: new initiation of a DPP-4 inhibitor

atoms.canonical_statement: Modified MACE was defined as a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, and all-cause death.

concept.text: Modified major adverse cardiovascular events (modified MACE)

outcome.definition: Composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, and all-cause death
outcome.measurement_method: Claims algorithms plus linked mortality sources

atoms.canonical_statement: Hospitalization for heart failure was a primary effectiveness outcome identified from inpatient diagnosis codes.
Hypovolemia was a prespecified safety outcome defined with claims-based diagnosis/procedure algorithms.
Genital infections was a prespecified safety outcome defined with claims-based diagnosis/procedure algorithms.
Diabetic ketoacidosis was a prespecified safety outcome defined with claims-based diagnosis/procedure algorithms.
Acute kidney injury was a prespecified safety outcome defined with claims-based diagnosis/procedure algorithms.
Lower-limb amputation was a prespecified safety outcome defined with claims-based diagnosis/procedure algorithms.

Propensity scores for SGLT2i initiation versus DPP-4i were estimated separately within each HbA1c subgroup using 128 prespecified covariates, followed by 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching with a 0.01 caliper.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: logistic regression model with 128 prespecified covariates

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary analysis used an as-treated follow-up beginning the day after cohort entry and censored at discontinuation, treatment change, outcome, death, disenrollment, or end of data.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Adopting an as-treated approach, the follow-up started the day after cohort entry

atoms.canonical_statement: After propensity-score matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced and the propensity-score distributions overlapped completely.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: all baseline characteristics were well balanced

atoms.canonical_statement: In the matched cohort, SGLT2i versus DPP-4i was associated with lower modified MACE risk: HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.75-0.95), with incidence rates 17.13 versus 20.18 per 1000 person-years.

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety sensitivity analyses that excluded patients with recent history of selected recurrent safety outcomes showed the same directional pattern; homogeneity P values remained >.05 except for genital infections.

atoms.canonical_statement: Residual confounding from unmeasured characteristics such as diabetes duration or body mass index could not be ruled out.
HbA1c stratification reduced precision for some subgroup outcome estimates, including modified MACE and DKA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: stratification by HbA1c levels reduced precision

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean on-treatment follow-up was shorter than in cardiovascular outcome trials, limiting direct long-term inference.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: mean follow-up (ie, time on treatment) was shorter compared with CVOTs

atoms.canonical_statement: Outcome misclassification could not be entirely excluded despite use of validated outcome definitions.

atoms.canonical_statement: Cardiovascular death could not be evaluated because cause-of-death information was unavailable, and all-cause death records could be incomplete.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that SGLT2i initiators had lower risks of MACE, HHF, and AKI and higher risks of genital infections and DKA than DPP-4i initiators, without meaningful variation by baseline HbA1c for most outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patients who initiated SGLT2i therapy had a reduced risk of MACE, HHF, and AKI
